name: Communication & Information Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations centred on transmitting, announcing and delivering information before electronic media.

name: Telegraph Operator
description: Operated an electrical telegraph, sending and receiving Morse-coded messages over land lines.

name: Morse Operator
description: Specialized in sending and receiving International Morse code at commercial speed.

name: Submarine Cable Operator
description: Worked the sensitive galvanometer instruments of an overseas telegraph cable station.

name: Switchboard Operator
description: Manually connected telephone calls by plugging cords into a switchboard jack field.

name: Town Crier
description: Publicly announced proclamations, news and court orders by ringing a bell and crying in the street.

name: Herald
description: Delivered royal and noble proclamations and oversaw ceremonial and armorial affairs.

name: Courier
description: Carried dispatches and letters over long distances on foot or horseback before regular postal service.

name: Post Rider
description: Rode a fixed relay route carrying official mail, changing horses at posting stations.

name: Semaphore Operator
description: Transmitted messages by positioning the arms of a semaphore tower or flag.

name: Heliograph Operator
description: Signalled with flashes of reflected sunlight using a heliograph mirror.

name: Flag Signalman
description: Conveyed tactical and railway messages using hand-held signal flags.

name: News Crier
description: Shouted headlines and hawked newspapers or broadsides in the street.

name: Carrier Pigeon Keeper
description: Bred, trained and dispatched homing pigeons for message delivery.

name: Telegram Messenger
description: Delivered telegrams on foot or bicycle from the telegraph office to recipients.

name: Wireless Operator
description: Operated early spark-gap radio equipment to send and receive Morse by electromagnetic waves.

name: Lector
description: Read aloud newspapers, literature and political texts to workers while they laboured, notably in cigar factories.

name: Scribal & Documentary Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of writing, copying and decorating documents by hand.

name: Scribe
description: Wrote and copied documents by hand as a professional penman.

name: Manuscript Scribe
description: Copied literary and religious manuscripts by hand in a scriptorium.

name: Legal Scribe
description: Drafted deeds, contracts and legal instruments by hand.

name: Temple Scribe
description: Kept temple records and sacred texts in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.

name: Court Scribe
description: Recorded decrees and archives for an imperial or royal court.

name: Illuminator
description: Decorated manuscripts with gold leaf, pigments and painted initials.

name: Miniaturist
description: Painted small detailed illustrations and portraits within manuscripts.

name: Rubricator
description: Drew red initials, headings and rubrics to structure a manuscript page.

name: Copyist
description: Reproduced texts and music by hand for distribution.

name: Scrivener
description: A professional copyist of legal and business documents.

name: Court Calligrapher
description: Produced official and artistic brush or pen writing for court documents.

name: Shorthand Writer
description: Recorded speech in abbreviated script for courts and parliaments.

name: Public Letter Writer
description: Composed and wrote letters for illiterate customers at a street stall.

name: Printing & Typesetting Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of composing, printing and binding text and images by hand.

name: Typesetter
description: Composed movable type by hand for letterpress printing.

name: Hand Compositor
description: Set individual type characters by hand into a composing stick.

name: Linotype Operator
description: Cast whole lines of type on a hot-metal Linotype machine.

name: Monotype Operator
description: Cast individual characters on a keyboard-driven Monotype caster.

name: Hand Press Printer
description: Inked type and pulled impressions on a hand-operated printing press.

name: Woodcut Carver
description: Cut relief images into wood blocks for printing illustrations.

name: Copperplate Engraver
description: Incised images into copper plates for intaglio printing.

name: Lithographer
description: Drew and printed images from prepared limestone using lithography.

name: Electrotyper
description: Deposited copper onto wax moulds by electrolysis to make durable plates.

name: Hand Bookbinder
description: Sewed, glued and bound printed sheets into books by hand.

name: Craft & Manufacture Occupations
description: Pre-industrial handicraft occupations grouped by material and trade.

name: Woodworking Occupations
description: Handicrafts of shaping, joining and turning wood.

name: Cooper
description: Made and repaired wooden barrels, casks and buckets.

name: Tight Cooper
description: Made liquid-tight barrels for wine, beer and other wet goods.

name: Dry Cooper
description: Made barrels for dry goods such as flour and tobacco.

name: White Cooper
description: Made straight-sided household vessels such as pails and churns.

name: Wheelwright
description: Built and repaired wooden spoked wheels for carts and wagons.

name: Wainwright
description: Constructed horse-drawn wagons and carts.

name: Pit Sawyer
description: Cut logs into boards by hand using a two-man pit saw.

name: Clog Maker
description: Carved wooden-soled footwear.

name: Broom Squire
description: Made brooms and besoms from birch twigs and heather.

name: Fletcher
description: Made and fletched arrows with feathers.

name: Bowyer
description: Crafted longbows and other wooden bows.

name: Metalworking Occupations
description: Handicrafts of forging, casting and finishing metal.

name: Blacksmith
description: Forged and shaped iron and steel by heating and hammering.

name: Farrier
description: Shod horses and treated their hooves.

name: Whitesmith
description: Finished and polished tin and light metalwork, often tinning surfaces.

name: Tinsmith
description: Fabricated household wares from tinplate.

name: Tinker
description: An itinerant mender of metal pots and pans.

name: Coppersmith
description: Raised and soldered copper vessels and pipes.

name: Pewterer
description: Cast and finished pewter tableware.

name: Bell Founder
description: Cast church and town bells in bronze.

name: Nailer
description: Forged nails by hand at a hearth, often as domestic outwork.

name: Swordsmith
description: Forged, tempered and polished swords.

name: Katana Smith
description: Forged and folded Japanese katana blades.

name: Armourer
description: Forged and fitted plate and mail armour.

name: Gunsmith
description: Bored, rifled and stocked early firearms.

name: Clockmaker
description: Hand-made and repaired mechanical clocks.

name: Watchmaker
description: Assembled and regulated pocket watches by hand.

name: Leatherworking Occupations
description: Handicrafts of tanning, dressing and sewing leather.

name: Tanner
description: Converted raw hides into leather using tannins.

name: Currier
description: Dressed, softened and finished tanned leather.

name: Cordwainer
description: Made fine leather shoes from new leather.

name: Cobbler
description: Repaired worn shoes.

name: Saddler
description: Made and repaired saddles and horse harness.

name: Furrier
description: Dressed and sewed furs into garments.

name: Parchmenter
description: Prepared animal skins into writing parchment and vellum.

name: Stone, Glass & Ceramic Occupations
description: Handicrafts of working stone, glass and fired clay.

name: Stone Mason
description: Cut, dressed and set stone for buildings.

name: Stone Carver
description: Carved decorative and monumental stonework.

name: Glassblower
description: Blew and shaped molten glass into vessels.

name: Potter
description: Threw and fired clay vessels on a wheel.

name: Brickmaker
description: Moulded and fired clay bricks.

name: Lime Burner
description: Calcined limestone in kilns to produce quicklime.

name: Flint Knapper
description: Struck flint to make gun flints and cutting tools.

name: Fiber, Paper & Basketry Occupations
description: Handicrafts of weaving fiber, forming paper and making small wares.

name: Hand Papermaker
description: Formed sheets of paper from rag pulp on a mould and deckle.

name: Basket Maker
description: Wove willow, rush or cane into baskets.

name: Ropemaker
description: Laid and twisted hemp into rope on a ropewalk.

name: Thatcher
description: Thatched roofs with straw, reed or rushes.

name: Chandlery & Soap Occupations
description: Handicrafts of making candles, soap and lighting fats.

name: Candle Maker
description: Dipped and moulded candles for lighting.

name: Tallow Chandler
description: Rendered animal fat into tallow candles and soap.

name: Wax Chandler
description: Made beeswax and spermaceti candles.

name: Rushlight Maker
description: Dipped peeled rushes in fat to make cheap rushlights.

name: Soap Boiler
description: Boiled fats and lye to make soap.

name: Textile & Garment Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of spinning, weaving, dyeing and sewing cloth and clothing.

name: Hand Spinner
description: Twisted fibres into yarn on a spindle or spinning wheel.

name: Handloom Weaver
description: Wove cloth on a hand or foot-treadle loom.

name: Fuller
description: Cleaned and thickened woollen cloth by treading or pounding in water.

name: Dyer
description: Coloured cloth and yarn with natural dyes.

name: Lace Maker
description: Worked bobbins or needles to make lace.

name: Embroiderer
description: Decorated fabric with needle and thread.

name: Tapestry Weaver
description: Wove pictorial hangings on a high-warp loom.

name: Hatter
description: Blocked and finished felt hats.

name: Milliner
description: Trimmed and sold women's hats and headwear.

name: Seamstress
description: Sewed garments by hand or on early machines.

name: Tailor
description: Cut and fitted bespoke garments by hand.

name: Dressmaker
description: Made women's gowns to measure.

name: Domestic & Personal Service Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of service within households and to individuals.

name: Footman
description: Attended a carriage, waited at table and ran errands in livery.

name: Running Footman
description: Ran ahead of a carriage to announce its arrival and clear the way.

name: Valet
description: A gentleman's personal attendant, caring for clothes and grooming.

name: Lady's Maid
description: A lady's personal servant, dressing hair and wardrobe.

name: Scullery Maid
description: Washed dishes and scrubbed the kitchen as the lowest-ranked maid.

name: Kitchen Maid
description: Prepared ingredients and assisted the cook.

name: Chambermaid
description: Cleaned and maintained bedrooms in a great house or hotel.

name: Butler
description: Managed the wine cellar and male household staff.

name: Groom
description: Cared for horses and drove carriages as required.

name: Nursemaid
description: Cared for the children of the household.

name: Wet Nurse
description: Breastfed another woman's infant for pay.

name: Governess
description: Educated the children of a wealthy household.

name: Laundress
description: Washed and ironed household linen and clothes.

name: Punkah-Wallah
description: Pulled a ceiling fan (punkah) by rope to cool a room.

name: Food & Provisioning Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of producing and vending food, drink and household provisions.

name: Ice Cutter
description: Sawed and harvested blocks of natural ice from frozen lakes.

name: Iceman
description: Delivered blocks of ice to homes and iceboxes.

name: Water Carrier
description: Carried and sold fresh water from wells or springs.

name: Milkmaid
description: Milked cows by hand and churned butter.

name: Dairymaid
description: Managed the dairy, making butter and cheese.

name: Milkman
description: Delivered fresh milk door to door by horse-drawn cart.

name: Baker
description: Kneaded and baked bread in a wood-fired oven.

name: Brewer
description: Brewed ale and beer by hand in small breweries.

name: Miller
description: Ground grain into flour at a water or wind mill.

name: Costermonger
description: Sold fruit and vegetables from a street barrow.

name: Peddler
description: Travelled selling small goods door to door.

name: Transport & Porterage Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of carrying people and goods by human or animal power.

name: Sedan Bearer
description: Carried passengers in an enclosed sedan chair.

name: Palanquin Bearer
description: Bore a covered palanquin for wealthy or noble passengers.

name: Rickshaw Puller
description: Hauled a two-wheeled passenger cart on foot.

name: Litter Bearer
description: Carried the sick or wounded on a stretcher-like litter.

name: Stagecoach Driver
description: Drove a scheduled passenger coach over fixed routes.

name: Coachman
description: Drove a private horse-drawn carriage.

name: Postilion
description: Rode the near horse of a carriage team to guide it.

name: Wagoner
description: Drove heavy freight wagons overland.

name: Carter
description: Hauled goods by horse and cart for hire.

name: Drayman
description: Delivered beer and heavy barrels by dray.

name: Teamster
description: Drove a team of oxen or mules hauling freight.

name: Muleteer
description: Led pack mules over mountain trails.

name: Camel Driver
description: Led camel caravans across desert routes.

name: Packhorse Driver
description: Guided trains of loaded packhorses.

name: Ferryman
description: Poled or rowed passengers across rivers.

name: Maritime & Waterway Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of working ships, coasts and inland waterways under sail and oar.

name: Whaler
description: Hunted whales from open boats for oil and baleen.

name: Harpooner
description: Cast the harpoon to fasten a whale.

name: Ship's Cooper
description: Made and repaired the barrels stowing a ship's provisions.

name: Ship Chandler
description: Supplied ships with provisions and nautical stores.

name: Sailmaker
description: Cut and sewed sails for square-rigged ships.

name: Ship Caulker
description: Drove oakum into plank seams and sealed them with pitch.

name: Oarsman
description: Rowed a galley or boat for propulsion.

name: Galley Slave
description: A convict or captive forced to row a war galley.

name: Powder Monkey
description: A boy who ferried gunpowder to a warship's guns.

name: Lamp Trimmer
description: Tended and refilled a ship's oil lamps and compass.

name: Lighthouse Keeper
description: Maintained the light and lived at an isolated lighthouse.

name: Lighterman
description: Transferred cargo between ship and shore in a lighter barge.

name: Bargeman
description: Worked a canal or river cargo barge.

name: Canal Boatman
description: Steered horse-drawn narrowboats on canals.

name: Agricultural & Pastoral Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of pre-mechanized farming, herding and rural extraction.

name: Reaper
description: Cut grain by hand with a sickle or scythe.

name: Scythesman
description: Mowed hay and grain with a long scythe.

name: Sheaf Binder
description: Gathered and bound cut grain into sheaves.

name: Thresher
description: Separated grain from stalks by flailing or treading.

name: Winnower
description: Tossed threshed grain to separate chaff in the wind.

name: Gleaner
description: Gathered leftover grain from harvested fields.

name: Ploughman
description: Guided a horse- or ox-drawn plough.

name: Haymaker
description: Cut, turned and stacked hay for winter fodder.

name: Shepherd
description: Tended grazing sheep and led them between pastures.

name: Swineherd
description: Herded pigs to woodland mast for foraging.

name: Cowherd
description: Tended and drove cattle.

name: Goatherd
description: Tended grazing goats.

name: Oxherd
description: Drove and yoked oxen for ploughing.

name: Turf Cutter
description: Cut peat or turf for fuel.

name: Charcoal Burner
description: Slow-burned wood in a kiln to make charcoal.

name: Fur Trapper
description: Trapped wild animals for the fur trade.

name: Historical Healing & Body Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of folk medicine, surgery and bodily care.

name: Barber-Surgeon
description: Cut hair, pulled teeth and performed surgery before the professions separated.

name: Apothecary
description: Compounded and sold medicines and simples.

name: Leech
description: A folk healer who practised bloodletting, named for the leech.

name: Leech Collector
description: Gathered medicinal leeches from ponds for sale to physicians.

name: Bonesetter
description: Set fractures and dislocations by manipulation.

name: Tooth Drawer
description: Extracted aching teeth at fairs and markets.

name: Plague Doctor
description: Treated plague victims wearing a beaked, herb-filled mask.

name: Midwife
description: Attended childbirth.

name: Herbalist
description: Gathered and dispensed medicinal herbs.

name: Bath Attendant
description: Served bathers at public bathhouses or hammams.

name: Proto-Scientific & Occult Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of speculative natural philosophy, divination and pseudoscience.

name: Alchemist
description: Sought transmutation and the philosopher's stone through proto-chemical practice.

name: Astrologer
description: Cast horoscopes and predicted events from the stars.

name: Augur
description: Interpreted the will of the gods from the flight of birds.

name: Haruspex
description: Read entrails of sacrificed animals to foretell outcomes.

name: Oracle
description: Delivered divine prophecies at a sacred shrine.

name: Diviner
description: Found water, minerals or answers by ritual means.

name: Dowser
description: Located underground water with a divining rod.

name: Necromancer
description: Purported to summon and question the dead.

name: Phrenologist
description: Read character from the shape and bumps of the skull.

name: Almanac Maker
description: Compiled calendars, weather and astrological predictions.

name: Religious & Ritual Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of priesthood, ritual and sacred service.

name: Vestal Virgin
description: A priestess of Vesta who tended Rome's sacred hearth fire.

name: Temple Priest
description: Performed sacrifices and rites at an ancient temple.

name: Hierophant
description: Revealed sacred mysteries at Eleusis.

name: Druid
description: A Celtic priest, judge and keeper of lore.

name: Anchorite
description: A recluse enclosed in a cell attached to a church for a life of prayer.

name: Sin Eater
description: Ritually consumed food over a corpse to absorb its sins.

name: Pardoner
description: Sold indulgences and relics in the medieval church.

name: Exorcist
description: Performed rituals to cast out spirits.

name: Entertainment & Performance Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of court, street and arena entertainment.

name: Court Jester
description: Amused the court with wit, mockery and foolery.

name: Minstrel
description: A travelling medieval entertainer and musician.

name: Troubadour
description: A poet-composer of courtly love songs in Occitania.

name: Jongleur
description: A wandering entertainer combining music, juggling and recitation.

name: Bard
description: A Celtic poet-singer who preserved genealogies and history.

name: Gleeman
description: An Anglo-Saxon itinerant entertainer and reciter.

name: Court Musician
description: Performed and composed music for a royal court.

name: Town Wait
description: A civic musician who played for the town and night watch.

name: Mummer
description: Performed masked folk plays at festivals.

name: Organ Grinder
description: Played a barrel organ in the street for coins.

name: Dancing Bear Handler
description: Trained and exhibited dancing bears.

name: Gladiator
description: Fought armed combat in Roman arenas for public spectacle.

name: Charioteer
description: Raced horse-drawn chariots in ancient circuses.

name: Bull Leaper
description: Vaulted over charging bulls in Minoan ritual sport.

name: Lighting & Urban Services Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of lighting, waking, cleaning and scavenging the pre-modern city.

name: Lamplighter
description: Lit and extinguished street gas lamps at dusk and dawn.

name: Link Boy
description: Carried a flaming torch to light pedestrians through dark streets.

name: Knocker-Up
description: Woke workers by tapping on windows with a long pole.

name: Night Watchman
description: Patrolled and guarded a town or premises by night.

name: Gong Farmer
description: Cleaned out privies and cesspits by night.

name: Night Soil Collector
description: Collected human waste for use as fertiliser.

name: Rat Catcher
description: Caught and killed rats, often with terriers and ferrets.

name: Chimney Sweep
description: Climbed and swept soot from chimneys.

name: Crossing Sweeper
description: Swept a path across muddy streets for pedestrians for tips.

name: Shoeblack
description: Polished boots and shoes on the street.

name: Mudlark
description: Scavenged the Thames foreshore for salvage.

name: Tosher
description: Searched Victorian sewers for coins and valuables.

name: Dustman
description: Collected household ash and refuse by cart.

name: Pre-Modern Military Occupations
description: Obsolete military roles of the age of bow, pike and edged weapons.

name: Archer
description: A soldier who fought with bow and arrows.

name: Longbowman
description: A soldier armed with the English longbow.

name: Crossbowman
description: A soldier armed with the crossbow.

name: Pikeman
description: A foot soldier armed with a long pike.

name: Musketeer
description: A soldier armed with a matchlock musket.

name: Arquebusier
description: A soldier armed with the early arquebus.

name: Cuirassier
description: A heavy cavalryman in breastplate armour.

name: Cataphract
description: A heavily armoured cavalryman of antiquity.

name: Knight
description: A mounted armoured warrior of the feudal nobility.

name: Samurai
description: A member of the Japanese warrior class.

name: Man-at-Arms
description: A heavily armed professional medieval soldier.

name: Cannon Founder
description: Cast bronze and iron cannon.

name: Standard Bearer
description: Carried the unit's banner into battle.

name: Administrative & Clerical Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of record-keeping, revenue and civic administration.

name: Tally Clerk
description: Kept accounts on notched wooden tally sticks.

name: Copying Clerk
description: Hand-copied letters and ledgers in offices.

name: Court Clerk
description: Recorded proceedings and drafted orders for a court.

name: Lictor
description: An attendant who escorted Roman magistrates carrying fasces.

name: Beadle
description: A parish or university officer who kept order and made proclamations.

name: Tax Farmer
description: Bought the right to collect taxes and profited from the yield.

name: Exciseman
description: Collected excise duties on goods and inspected for smuggling.

name: Gatekeeper
description: Controlled entry at a castle or city gate.

name: Summoner
description: Served summonses to appear before an ecclesiastical court.

name: Quipu Keeper
description: Recorded Inca accounts on knotted cords (quipu).

name: Imperial Examiner
description: Graded candidates in the imperial civil-service examinations.

name: Industrial Era Obsolete Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of the early industrial mills, mines and manual machinery.

name: Mule Spinner
description: Operated the spinning mule in cotton mills.

name: Power Loom Weaver
description: Tended power looms in textile mills.

name: Carder
description: Prepared fibres by carding before spinning.

name: Piecer
description: A child who joined broken threads in spinning mills.

name: Doffer
description: Removed full bobbins from spinning frames, often a child.

name: Mill Scavenger
description: A child who crawled under machines to clear waste.

name: Breaker Boy
description: A boy who sorted impurities from coal at the breaker.

name: Hurrier
description: A child who hauled coal tubs through mine tunnels.

name: Mine Trapper
description: A child who opened and closed mine ventilation doors.

name: Navvy
description: A labourer who built canals, railways and roads.

name: Stoker
description: Fed coal into steam-engine and ship boilers.

name: Match Girl
description: Dipped matches, often suffering phosphorus poisoning.

name: Pin Boy
description: Reset bowling pins by hand between frames.

name: Elevator Operator
description: Drove a manual lever elevator and announced floors.

name: Computing, Film & Reproduction Occupations
description: Obsolete occupations of manual computation, data entry and photographic reproduction.

name: Human Computer
description: Performed mathematical calculations by hand or with tables.

name: Astronomical Computer
description: Computed star tables and orbital data by hand.

name: Keypunch Operator
description: Punched data into cards on a keypunch machine.

name: Tabulating Machine Operator
description: Ran punched-card tabulators for censuses and accounts.

name: Comptometer Operator
description: Entered figures on a key-driven mechanical adding machine.

name: Film Projectionist
description: Threaded and ran motion-picture projectors in cinemas.

name: Darkroom Technician
description: Developed and printed photographs in a darkroom.

name: Magic Lanternist
description: Projected painted glass slides with a magic lantern.
